subject: Private Deploy: BYO-K + operator telemetry carve-out for Medisys
messages:
From: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@medisys.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Medisys Legal <legal@medisys.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on private deployment BYO-K + operator telemetry

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the performance numbers. Before we start procurement, our legal and privacy teams have a couple of questions about the Private Deployment option:

1) BYO-K: we need explicit guarantees that customer-controlled keys (CMKs) will be used for model input encryption at rest and for any persisted KV cache.
2) Operator telemetry: Medisys requires a narrow telemetry envelope. We need to know what operator metrics Redwood collects, whether any inference input/query fragments are logged outside the VPC, and whether there is a built-in carve-out to redact or summarize telemetry before it leaves the private network.
3) Subprocessors: please provide a list of subprocessors that have access to operator tooling for private deployments and the conditions under which they may be engaged (e.g., breakglass).

Attached is a short checklist from our privacy team; can you route this to engineering and legal? We want to align on the DPA redlines and any needed contractual language for keys/telemetry before SOW sign.

Appreciate a short call — are you available 1/12 or 1/13?

Best,
Sophie Lambert
Head of IT Security, Medisys Health
(attachment: medisys_privacy_checklist.pdf)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@medisys.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment BYO-K + operator telemetry

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (security) and Irene (legal) to scope the answers and map to DPA redlines.

Quick summary of what we can confirm up front:
- BYO-K: Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) support customer-managed keys. Customer CMKs are used for snapshot storage and for persisted KV caches; runtime models operating in the node memory do not require key unwrap outside the node.
- Telemetry: by default we send aggregated health and infra metrics to Redwood SaaS control plane; no raw input/query text is transmitted. For Medisys we can configure a telemetry carve-out: only rolling counters and anonymized latency/error histograms are sent, and raw request traces are suppressed unless a breakglass incident is declared.
- Subprocessors: we use a small set of subprocessors for host OS patching and private deployment orchestration (listed below). Any human access to customer workloads is tied to an audited breakglass procedure and scoping addendum.

Proposed next steps:
1) Karthik and Irene will produce a 1-page technical binding that maps the telemetry whitelist and EXACT fields we will collect.
2) We will provide a subprocessors appendix and a draft contractual addendum for operator access windows.
3) If this looks right, schedule a 30m call to walk legal through the DPA touchpoints.

We have availability 1/12 at 10:30am PT — does that work?

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
(attachments: none)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@medisys.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment BYO-K + operator telemetry

Sophie — following up with the telemetry whitelist and subprocessors list. Summary below; I'll attach a short technical note to the shared Drive.

Telemetry whitelist (default for Medisys private deploy):
- Node health: CPU/mem utilization (percent), GPU temperature, disk pressure (no payloads)
- Inference meta: request id, model version, token count, latency bucket, error code
- Aggregates only: 1-minute rolling counters; no request-level request bodies or prompt fragments

Operator access and subprocessors:
- Subprocessors that may be involved:
  - CloudPatchOps Inc. (OS patching automation) — has no access to application-layer artifacts; host-level only; under NDA
  - EdgeProvisioning LLC (deployment orchestration agent) — may receive encrypted service account tokens; never receives plain-text customer data or keys
  - RemoteDebug Partners (on-call escalations) — access only via time-boxed breakglass and recorded session; their participation is governed by addendum and explicit customer approval

Breakglass conditions:
- Customer initiates or approves a session via a signed ticket; access is time-limited, recorded, and limited to a scoped runbook. All sessions require customer auditor token approval except in legally compelled emergency scenarios where Redwood will notify customer within 24 hours.

Attaching: a one-page telemetry matrix (priv-deploy-telemetry-matrix.pdf) and a subprocessors appendix (subprocessors_med.pdf).

-Karthik
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachments: priv-deploy-telemetry-matrix.pdf, subprocessors_med.pdf)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@medisys.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Medisys Legal <legal@medisys.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 13:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment BYO-K + operator telemetry

Sophie / Medisys Legal — attaching our suggested edits to the DPA that address: key custody (BYO-K obligations and KMS audit), telemetry scope and redaction, and operator breakglass language. Major changes called out in the comments:
- Clause 4.2 (Encryption and Key Custody): added explicit requirement that Redwood will not retain plaintext customer keys; KMS operations that require key unwrap will occur inside the customer-controlled HSM boundary or on the private node under customer CMKs.
- Clause 6.1 (Telemetry): tightened telemetry to exclude any pseudonymizable prompt material; allowed aggregated health metrics and model-level counters only.
- Clause 9.3 (Subprocessors & Breakglass): added 48hr prior notice for non-emergency subprocessors and a documented customer approval workflow for manual vendor sessions.

Please see the attached redline: Medisys_DPA_redlines_v2.docx. The next step from a contract perspective is a short call to walk through the changes and confirm acceptable SLAs for operator sessions (max session length, retention of recordings, and audit log export cadence).

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
(attachment: Medisys_DPA_redlines_v2.docx)

Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment BYO-K + operator telemetry

Irene / Priya — quick update from Medisys Legal after an internal review: the majority of your redlines are acceptable. A few follow-ups before we finalize:

1) Add an explicit retention cap for breakglass session recordings (we propose 90 days with certified deletion)
2) Confirm the technical control that ensures KV cache snapshots are encrypted with the customer CMK and that any snapshot export routine requires customer-signed approval
3) A short appendix listing subprocessors and their access categories (host-only, orchestration, breakglass-only) — if you can supply this in spreadsheet form, it will speed procurement.

We can take the appendix offline; if you can accept items (1) and (2) we will sign an MOA and move to SOW. I'll target legal to produce countersign redlines by EOD 1/19. Thanks for the quick turnaround — looking forward to finalizing.

Best,
Sophie Lambert
Head of IT Security, Medisys Health
